title: Vulnerability Pipeline Retrospective - notes and next steps
body:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Riley, Sofia, Devon, + quick sync from Product (Anya)

Goals for this retro
- Surface why we had a spike in 'low-confidence' secret findings last sprint
- Decide runway for threat-modeling on the new "Dedicated autoscaling" feature
- Tune the vuln pipeline: triage SLAs, signal-to-noise improvements, and backlog cleanup

Quick context
- Last 2 weeks: scanner noise up ~3x (false positives on base64 blobs in logs), blocking flow slowed.
- On-call SREs spent ~5 hours triaging alerts that were later marked FP.
- Threat-modeling kickoff for autoscaling feature scheduled for 2026-06-08.

Notes / Observations (raw)
- Secrets scanner is flagging environment dumps in crash logs — many of these are developer sandboxes (local) that get uploaded to test buckets.
- We lack a good denylist for common CI artifacts (e.g., GITHUB_ACTIONS, NETLIFY) — causes noise.
- Some vulnerable dependency alerts (Dependabot) are low priority but overflowed team's mailbox because of noisy label rules.
- Our current triage SLAs: 24h for Severity P1, 72h P2. P2 breaches increased this sprint.
- Threat modeling readiness: product has partial designs, no sequence diagrams yet. Need attacker goals doc.
- KB (Confluence) playbook sections are outdated: screenshots reference old console UI.

Decisions made in the meeting
- Short-term: add CI artifact denylist to secrets-scanner by Jun 4 (Riley, SE-1123).
- Medium-term: introduce a 'confidence' header from the scanner so triage UI can filter <0.6 by default (Marco, infra PR 889).
- Triage SLA change: keep P1 at 24h, reduce P2 to 48h for next two sprints and re-evaluate (Sofia will propose staffing adjustments).
- Threat-modeling: split into two workshops — system-level (attacker surface) and component-level (KV cache + autoscaler). Product to provide diagrams by Jun 2 (Anya).

Action items (owner, ticket, due)
- Riley: implement CI artifact denylist and deploy to staging. Ticket: SE-1123. Due: 2026-06-04.
- Marco: open infra PR to add scanner "confidence" header + UI flag to hide low-confidence findings. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/889. Due: 2026-06-07.
- Sofia: update triage rota and propose two extra on-call shifts for P2 coverage. Ticket: SEC-2045. Due: 2026-06-06.
- Devon: update Vulnerability Playbook Confluence pages (screenshots, workflow steps) and add a small how-to for false-positive tagging. Due: 2026-06-10.
- Aisha: draft attacker-goals doc for autoscaling feature and share with Product. Due: 2026-06-01.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How to handle developer sandbox uploads to shared test buckets: policy vs tooling? (spoke with infra — need bucket lifecycle/ACL audit) => follow-up with Platform Eng.
- Should low-confidence findings be auto-archived after 30 days if no activity? Pros/cons discussed — lean towards archiving but need metrics.
- Are there privacy/regulatory concerns if we start auto-archiving so quickly? Legal to weigh in (Theresa).

Metrics to track next sprint
- FP rate for secrets scanner (baseline: 72% FP last sprint) — target: reduce to <=45% in 4 sprints.
- Mean time to first triage (MTFT) for P2 — baseline: 52h — target: <=36h next sprint.
- Number of Dependabot alerts flagged / merged vs ignored — measure noise reduction.

Quick reference: triage checklist (notes-to-self style)
- Confirm reproducible exploit path? yes/no
- Is this an alert on prod only or dev/test as well?
- Check commit author + CI job — is it an automated commit from dependabot?
- Apply "false-positive" tag with reason and short note if FP.
- If P1: escalate to SRE lead and create incident stub.

Misc / side notes
- Riley: observed that the scanner regex for AWS keys is too broad — created a small regex refinement proposal.
- Marco: infra team will batch low-confidence results nightly into a digest for team leads to review.
- Anya (Product): will prep sequence diagrams for autoscaling; wants a short pre-read by Jun 4.

Risks
- Continued high FP rate causes alert fatigue and might obscure real signals.
- Threat modeling delay could push security gating later in the dev cycle for Dedicated autoscaling — want to avoid last-minute rework.

Follow-ups scheduled
- Quick sync next Tue (2026-06-02) to check progress on denylist + attacker-goals draft.
- Threat-modeling workshops: 2026-06-08 (system-level) and 2026-06-15 (component-level).

Notes to self
- Add a short demo for the team showing how to mark false-positive and update Confluence steps.
- Consider a monthly "scanner tuning" slot in team retro.

End of notes.
